acceptance: The skill is under 1,500 characters of instructions plus commands, and each command in it is run in a clean environment with its output shown in the PR.
The first command works from an environment with only the documented install step; the install step names the extra that provides a database driver.
Every methodological sentence maps to the published methodology page; the PR lists the mapping.
The skill has a name distinct from the contributor skill 'benchbox', lives outside the skill-sync managed mirrors, and scripts/check_untracked_skill_mirrors.sh passes.

The CLI-only arm of the gate's coding-agent probe is rerun with the skill within any remaining budget and the change in sound reports is recorded; if no budget remains, the PR says it was not measured.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence: core dependencies include no database driver and the quick-start extra installs only Polars, so the bare command 'benchbox run --platform duckdb' fails in a fresh environment unless the CLI installs the driver itself (not checked).

Decision gate: read the gate ruling first; on no-go, do nothing and ask the owner to drop the item. On go, decide and record where the skill is published (site docs, the package, or a plugin listing) before writing it; writing instructions into a user's own agent files is out of scope.

Verification rubric: pass only if every command was executed as written and no claim lacks a methodology-page source.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. One PR per item, squash-merged to develop (site work: one PR in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site). Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.
description:
Problem: an agent with a shell but no BenchBox MCP server has no always-loaded guidance, and models do not know the BenchBox CLI from training. A skill is the standard way to teach an unfamiliar CLI at low context cost.

Outcome: one short skill for end users (not contributors) covering the first working command, how to choose scale and iterations for a stated purpose, validating a run, comparing two runs, and what to report. Every claim comes from the methodology page.

Gate: do not start unless agent-reach-evidence-gate-20261112 ruled go for this item, or the owner overrides in writing on this item.
drop_reason: Dropped by owner decision on 2026-11-13: its go signal measured discovery, which a skill the user must install cannot fix. No successor.
